1.why: The sans-serif type is legible with comfortable line height throughout, though letter spacing is default rather than notably generous.

2.why: All instructions are in sentence case with no italics and no dense paragraphs; the only all-caps text is the 'NORTHSTAR BANK' brand header, not an instruction.

3.why: The single-column card layout, large buttons and short lines would fit a phone screen, although the monospace Logs panel wraps densely.

4.why: Every instruction is one or two plain sentences, e.g. 'Enter the delivered six-digit code.' and 'Store these codes somewhere safe.'

5.why: Only the recovery-code input shows a format example (placeholder 'ABCDE-FGHIJ'); the email, phone, verification-code and authenticator-code fields show none.

6.why: The user reads at most one or two short sentences of instruction per step; the only long text is the supplementary Logs panel rather than required prose.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control exists anywhere; the secret and recovery codes are shown only as plain text and must be re-typed by hand into the verification fields.

8.why: The authenticator setup offers only the manual secret string ('Manual secret: zfOdAqAvBRWgTD0p-WPGgY3FkX4') with no QR code or equivalent alternative.

9.why: Plain labelled inputs would accept generic browser autofill for email/phone, but nothing observable (autocomplete attributes, one-time-code support) demonstrates autofill or password-manager support for the code fields.

10.why: Each screen pairs a bold heading ('Sign in', 'Verify identity', 'Authenticator') with a high-contrast blue primary button, though the dashboard shows two identically styled blue buttons that compete for attention.

11.why: Several screens demand multiple main actions at once, e.g. the Authenticator screen (generate secret plus enter and confirm a code) and the dashboard (verify recovery code, regenerate codes, log out).

12.why: Status lines such as 'Recovery code accepted. Remaining unused codes: 7.' and 'Your authenticator is now enrolled.' plainly state what happened, and each following screen states the next step.

13.why: Codes can be regenerated and forms retried without visible penalty (the sign-in form persists after the error), but there are no reveal/hide toggles for any code or secret.

14.why: The only error shown, 'We could not complete that request.', avoids blaming the user but states neither the specific problem nor how to fix it.

15.why: Reading has no time limit, but the TOTP code explicitly expires ('expires at 19:55:30'), imposing a short, non-generous window for entering codes.
